intent: Take the five pacman_hook_stall libs off the shell-coverage allowlist, now that the fixed instrument measures each at 100.00% twice, taking the allowlist from 103 entries to 98.
scope: Non-goal: pacman_hook_stall_setup.sh, which measures 26/27 = 96.30% and stays allowlisted
Non-goal: the 16 untested libs in fixes/lib, which keep their explicit entries
changes: Each was measured twice through fixes/lib/tests/run_all.sh, the subject is_covered() builds, with the second run gating at --min 100 so a shortfall would have been a non-zero exit rather than a number to read.

verification.evidence: capture 59/59, load 25/25, summary 18/18, watch 24/24, usage 1/1 -- all 100.00%.

verification.command: the same five at --min 100, second independent run on a clean tree
verification.evidence: All five PASS with identical numbers: 59/59, 25/25, 18/18, 24/24, 1/1. Two matching runs was the bar set because fixes/lib's suites drive watch_forever timing loops and a timing-dependent suite could vary its line set; dwm_config.sh was seen to vary. These did not.

risks: usage.sh's denominator is 1, because the lib is a single usage() whose body is one `cat <<EOF` heredoc plus `exit 0` and heredoc content is data rather than statements. The 100.00% is honest but covers one line; the tests assert on the rendered text, so the behaviour is genuinely exercised.

summary.sh has one off-set line (36) -- a line the trace saw run that kcov never listed. That cannot inflate the number (an off-set line is by construction an executed line), but it means the lib is measured over a subset of its statements.
These libs are only enforced once check_shell_coverage.sh is wired into a hook, which still waits for the allowlist to reach zero.
rollback: git revert this commit to restore the five entries; nothing else depends on their absence.
After rollback, confirm check_shell_coverage.sh on any of the five exits 0 again by exemption rather than by coverage.
